title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the setup from p.78 (ms. p.12) inside Grothendieck's 'conformal surgery' programme. He compares two kinds of moduli stacks ('multiplicités modulaires'), each mapping to a purely combinatorial category, and draws two commutative triangles.

Case 1 (the triangle with toric data).
- MDB_{g,ν} is the moduli stack of compact holomorphic surfaces with boundary (B) of type (g,ν), 'disked' (D), i.e. carrying an admissible system of conformal disks/annuli.
- M_stND_{g,ν} is the moduli stack of stable curves of type (g,ν). Each node carries a 'propagator' structure (N): on the next page this is a nonzero element u_i ∈ T_{x'}⊗T_{x''}, or dually a pairing of the two tangent lines at the node. This is exactly a plumbing or smoothing parameter. Each marked point carries a disk; on the next page it is a round disk in the tangent line, so one positive real parameter.
- The arrow MDB → M_stND pinches the annuli of the disk system to nodes and records their conformal moduli as propagators.
- Both stacks map to mdt_{g,ν}: the category of Mumford–Deligne (modular) graphs, with genus weights at vertices and 'toric structures' (C^*/S^1 data) on the edges. The 't' records these toric structures in the combinatorial types.
- Dimension: real dimension equals that of C^{3g-3+ν} × R^ν, i.e. 6g-6+3ν. This is right for genus-g surfaces with ν unparametrized boundary circles. It is also right for stable curves with a radius at each marked point. On each stratum with k nodes, the k complex propagators restore the k complex dimensions lost.

Case 2 (the triangle without disks).
- Drop the disk structures. Boundary is absent, or a 'generalized boundary' shrunk to the ν points.
- One gets MD_{g,ν} → M_stN_{g,ν} over md_{g,ν} (modular graphs without toric data). The morphisms are now of C-algebraic multiplicities, of complex dimension 3g-3+ν.

Purpose. The next page asks whether the horizontal arrows are isomorphisms and how to construct inverses. The intended inverse is classical plumbing: from u_i and a chosen disk D'_i in T_{x'}, get the complementary disk D''_i in T_{x''} and glue. The page is thus a stack-theoretic, graph-indexed formulation of plumbing/sewing coordinates near the boundary of \bar M_{g,ν}.
errors: Naively, M_stN_{g,ν} is a disjoint union over strata of punctured normal bundles (nonzero u_e in T'⊗T'' per edge). As a plain algebraic stack this cannot be isomorphic to the irreducible M_{g,ν}; for example M_{0,4} versus M_{0,4} together with three copies of C^*. The question 'are the arrows isomorphisms?' only makes sense with a finer structure (fibered over md, analytic/tubular gluing, or the disk data of case 1). The page does not specify this.
The claim that the case-2 arrows are C-algebraic is asserted without construction. Plumbing is intrinsically analytic, and only the combinatorial-type maps are obviously algebraic.
The dimension count is correct: real 6g-6+3ν in case 1, complex 3g-3+ν in case 2.

ideas.what: Moduli stacks of stable curves with a node-smoothing parameter u ∈ T_{x'}⊗T_{x''} at each node ('propagators'), mapped to/from bordered Riemann surfaces
ideas.modern_name: plumbing / sewing coordinates; punctured normal bundles of boundary strata; log-smooth curves (Kato), Kato–Nakayama space of \bar M_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Plumbing: Fay, Kra, Earle–Marden, Wolpert. Sewing in physics: Zwiebach, Segal, Huang. Log viewpoint: F. Kato, Kato–Nakayama
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and tubular neighbourhoods of the boundary strata of \bar M_{g,ν}, but not this explicit propagator stack as far as known

ideas.what: Fibering moduli stacks over a category of Mumford–Deligne (modular) graphs with genus weights at vertices and toric structures on edges
ideas.modern_name: modular graphs/modular operads; graphs decorated with S^1 or C^* edge data (decorated/framed moduli)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998); Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov (1995, moduli with tangent-direction data at nodes)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Mumford–Deligne stratification, Teichmüller tower)

ideas.what: Dimension count: bordered or disked moduli of real dimension 6g-6+3ν; marked-point version of complex dimension 3g-3+ν
ideas.modern_name: dimension of moduli of bordered Riemann surfaces

missed.claim: The page organizes the bordered-surface / nodal-curve-with-smoothing-parameters correspondence as a morphism of stacks over a category of modular graphs with toric edge structures, using the physics word 'propagateurs'. This anticipates the modular-operad and sewing picture of string field theory, Segal CFT and Getzler–Kapranov, and the S^1-decorated-node moduli of Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov, a decade earlier.
missed.quote: dans mdt, la lettre t rappelle qu'on a inclus des structures toriques dans les types combinatoires
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precursor showing Grothendieck independently arrived at the plumbing/modular-operad framework while pursuing the anabelian Teichmüller tower. It suggests a direct link between his tower and the operadic and log-geometric (Kato–Nakayama) descriptions of the boundary of \bar M_{g,n}.

missed.claim: The question whether MDB → M_stND and MD → M_stN are isomorphisms, with an inverse via a canonical disk system from hyperbolic metrics, is posed and left open (continued on the next page).
missed.quote: MD_{g,ν} → M_stN_{g,ν} ... cette fois des morphismes de multiplicités C-algébriques
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A canonical (hyperbolic) choice of plumbing disks giving a global equivalence is related to modern 'canonical collar' and Kontsevich–Soibelman/Costello-type constructions. The precise stacky statement remains unformulated in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, early (1983–84), stacky and graph-indexed formulation of plumbing with 'propagators' and toric edge data, anticipating modular operads and decorated-node moduli. However, the underlying mathematics (plumbing, dimension counts) is classical, and the page is a sketch with an unresolved isomorphism question.
transcription_corrections: 'des structures toriques dans la façon considérée' should read 'des structures toriques dans les types combinatoires'.
'sans structure {+multi,+} discoïde' should read 'sans structure multi-discoïde'.

The last lines should read roughly: 'Dans le cas 1), les dimensions (réelles) sont celles de C^{3g-3+ν} × R^ν ; dans le cas 2), les dims. complexes sont celles de C^{3g-3+ν}'. The inserted '(réelles)' qualifies the case-1 dimensions; '(des pts et d'autres sont' is a misreading.
'Si au contraire [?], si on' is probably 'Si au contraire, si on'.
The page number 79 at the bottom is the folio number.
